New Community Authority (NCA) New Community Authorities (NCAs) are authorized under Section 349 of the Ohio Revised Code as a mechanism for creating well-planned and economically sustainable new communities. They are separate political subdivisions governed by a board of trustees. Establishing an NCA requires the filing of a petition, property owner consent, and approval from the municipal council. The municipal council then appoints a board of trustees to govern the NCA. Multiple NCAs can be formed in a municipality based on development needs. Once established, an NCA has the authority to issue bonds for specific projects, such as road construction or community facility development, funded through special taxes within the designated NCA area. COMMUNITY REINVESTMENT AREA (CRA) PROGRAM The main purpose of the CRA is to encourage development, redevelopment, and revitalization in the community so as to improve economic stability, maintain property values, and create new opportunities for growth and employment. The CRA provides a temporary tax abatement of increased real property taxes on significant remodeling or new construction within an eligible area. These tax abatements are considered on a case - by - case basis for new construction or rehabilitation of commerc ial or industrial properties that lead directly to job creation and/or retention within one of the CRA areas. Residential properties are not considered for abatements except for within the Uptown District CRA. Eligibility There are three CRAs in Plain City: Uptown District, US - 42 North, and US - 42 South. Relocation Notice A business that intends to fully or partially relocate from another community in Ohio must notify the Village at the time of application. The notification must include an explanation of the reason(s) for the relocation. The Village must then notify the original community and the Director of the Ohio Department of Development about the potential relocation at least 30 days prior to formal approval by Village Council.
